page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-8 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine featuring an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor. This instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 38 MB of L3 cache, supporting advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptography extensions. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core.

A defining feature of this server is the integration of a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, which is bundled with 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. This instance does not include any local NVMe SSD storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes. It also includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a clear division between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. The CPU exhibits weak single-core and multi-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench tests, alongside lower-tier compression and decompression speeds. However, memory bandwidth remains average, with read speeds reaching up to 351.55 GB/sec for cached blocks and 50.64 GB/sec for uncached blocks. Crucially, the server excels in machine learning tasks, achieving top-tier performance in LLM inference benchmarks. For a 7B parameter model, it processes prompts at 2225.82 tokens per second and generates text at 52.31 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g2-standard-8 offers a specialized hardware profile where the primary value resides in its Ada Lovelace GPU and high VRAM density relative to the 8 vCPU compute allocation. It is highly optimized for workloads such as low-latency LLM inference, small-to-medium AI model serving, and GPU-accelerated graphics rendering. It is less suitable for general-purpose CPU-heavy compilation or high-throughput database operations that do not leverage the GPU.
description: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-8 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine designed for GPU-accelerated workloads. It features an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and 32.0 GB of system memory. The server is equipped with a single NVIDIA L4 GPU from the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing 24 GB of dedicated VRAM, though it lacks local SSD storage. Benchmark data indicates weak single-core and multi-core CPU performance, but outstanding top-tier capabilities in large language model inference, processing 7B model prompts at 2225.82 tokens per second. This instance is highly efficient for machine learning inference, AI model serving, and graphics rendering workloads that leverage dedicated GPU acceleration rather than raw CPU compute power.
